newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks end firmer on bottom-fishing.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks end firmer on bottom-fishing.

text.p: Singapore shares ended mostly firmer in moderately active trade on Friday, underpinned by bargain-hunting in selected blue chips, dealers said.
"It's bottom-fishing, mainly. Sentiment has also improved though not across the board," said a dealer with a local house.
Dealers said renewed buying was noted in the foreign tranches of banks like OUB, OCBC, UOB and DBS which dominated the gainers' list, ending firmber by between S$0.50-0.60 each.
Keppel Corp, which had been sold recently, also same some buying. Shares of the shipping conglomerate rise five cents to S$6.35 on brisk turnover of three million shares.
Dealers said Keppel's buying was fuelled by news of its takeover of a Philippines bank. However, analysts felt the deal was unlikely to have any immediate earning contributions.
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended 11.97 points up at 2,016.23. Market volume was 138 million shares with 236 gainers and 103 losers.

Venture Manufacturing rose over seven percent to S$4.40 on the back of its recent upgrade to mainboard. Dealers said the boost could be linked to the fact that the firm was also currently on a roadshow to foreign investors.
Malaysian stocks were actively traded, pushing the UOB-OTC index up 17.08 points to 1,177.86.
